messages:
mike-support: FYI — ACME reports a 403 in the Console when they try to open Dedicated > Deployments > private model 'acme-prod-1'. Happens for multiple users after they were moved between Okta groups during a restructure. They can still call the API directly (hosted endpoints succeed), but console UI calls return 403. Customer says only project-level actions are blocked, billing/usage pages load fine. 

tara-ops: Can you paste exact repro steps and a curl that gets the 403? Also any x-request-id from the UI response?

mike-support: Repro steps from the customer: 1) Sign in via Okta SSO. 2) Switch org -> select project acme-prod-1. 3) Click Deployments -> click the private deployment row -> "Open" -> UI shows toast "403 permission denied".

They ran this curl and got 403: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "X-Org-Id: org_ACME123" \
  https://console.redwood.ai/api/internal/projects/acme-prod-1/deployments/acme-prod-1/private/open
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"forbidden","message":"caller not authorized for project action"}
```

x-request-id from their UI logs: `rq_0b9f7c3a`

siva: Thanks — this smells like role shadowing / project-level binding mismatch. After the Okta move did they switch to a different SCIM group that maps only to an org-level role? If their project access was via an intermediate service account or a delegated role, that could be orphaned.

tara-ops: @siva can you check the org -> project bindings for org_ACME123? Also check if any service-account role bindings reference a now-deleted group id.

emma: Quick triage checklist: 
- Verify the user's token scopes: `scopes` should include `project:read,project:deploy` for console actions. 
- Check membership via SCIM cache snapshot for org_ACME123 at the time of incident. 
- Look for a project-level binding that has `source: inherited_from_group` vs `direct_assignment`.

siva: Pulled the bindings. Findings: project acme-prod-1 has two role bindings: 
1) `project:viewer` assigned to Okta group `ACME-Eng` (now active) 
2) `project:deployer` assigned to service account `svc-acme-deploy` which had an inherited mapping to SCIM group id `00g9-oldgroup` — that SCIM group was removed in the Okta move. The service account still exists but its group link is dead, so effective permissions vanish for console flows that require `project:deployer`. API calls that use a different token path (api-key) still worked because their API key was scoped at org level.

josh: Created a ticket and a short mitigation plan. deploy-bot: Ticket created INC-7241 for eng-sre.

deploy-bot: {"ticket":"INC-7241","assignee":"eng-sre","severity":"high","x-request-id":"rq_0b9f7c3a"}

emma: Temporary workarounds we can propose to ACME: 
- Re-assign `project:deployer` directly to the user or to a currently-mapped Okta group via the Console (fast but manual). 
- Recreate the SCIM group with the old id and rebind (if they have a backup). 
- Run a manual role rebind script from our admin API: 
```
POST /admin/v1/projects/acme-prod-1/bindings
Body: {"principal":"group:okta:ACME-Eng","role":"project:deployer"}
```

mike-support: ACME prefers a painless route — they asked us not to create groups on their IdP. Want us to rebind on our side if possible.

siva: I can do a safe rebind: add a direct `project:deployer` binding for svc-acme-deploy -> but mark as `source: temporary_admin_fix` so it can be audited and removed after they finalize Okta groups. Will log the change and include rollback commands.

josh: Please include audit metadata and ping customer when done. I'll add the incident note.

siva: Executed patch at 2025-06-18T16:07:10Z: 
```
PATCH /admin/v1/projects/acme-prod-1/bindings/svc-acme-deploy
{ "role":"project:deployer", "source":"temporary_admin_fix", "meta":{"ticket":"INC-7241","changed_by":"siva"} }
```
Result: 200 OK, binding active. Audit id `audit_9c3b`

mike-support: Pushed update to ACME. They re-tested and report console open works now, no more 403. :tada:

ACME follow-up note (via support): "Confirmed — Deploy button restored for all affected users. Would like a long-term fix to avoid manual rebinds during future Okta reorganizations."

emma: Long-term recommendation for customer: use explicit group-to-role mapping docs we published (link internal) and enable SCIM preservation of group ids during migrations. For platform: we should add a health check that flags role bindings whose `principal` group_id no longer exists in the SCIM cache (opens INC-7241-2).

josh: Closing loop — I'll update the ticket with RCA: Okta group deletion caused service account's inherited binding to orphan -> effective project deployer role removed -> console 403 for flows that require that role. Action items: customer guidance + platform health check.

mike-support: Customer acked and asked to keep ticket open for a week for monitoring. Closing thread here but keeping INC-7241 open.
